He hums while he waits, badly.} Wait him out in the stacks {You crouch behind the history shelves for an hour, reading by the light of his lantern, until he gives up and goes to bed.|You wait him out, and he eats the whole sandwich first. Your knees will never forgive you.|You know his humming now. When it stops, he's asleep on his feet, and you slip past.} Bluff your way past {You tell him a professor is looking for him in the east tower. He goes. You are inside before his lantern reaches the stair.|"Thorne wants you," you say, and Bram's face goes pale. Nobody checks whether Thorne wants them.|You tell him there's a fight in the courtyard. There isn't. He's gone before you finish the sentence.} {"Nice try," says Bram, and writes your name in his little book with great pleasure.|He laughs, actually laughs, and walks you back to your dormitory by the ear.|Bram has heard that one before, from you. He takes your name, and his time over it.}
